questions.question: What does each row of a permutation matrix contain?
options: Exactly one entry equal to $1$, others zero.
Any entries as long as the row sum is zero.

questions.question: What does each column of a permutation matrix contain?
options: At least one arbitrary nonzero entry.
Exactly one diagonal entry equal to zero.

questions.question: Why must a permutation matrix be square?
options: Only square matrices can contain zeros.
Rectangular matrices cannot be multiplied by vectors.
A matrix with ones must always be square.
It represents a rearrangement of the same number of coordinates.

questions.question: Why is the identity matrix a permutation matrix?
options: One $1$ in each row and each column.
It swaps every pair of rows.
It has all entries equal to $1$.

questions.question: What does left multiplication by a permutation matrix do to a matrix?
options: It changes every entry to its negative.

questions.question: Which matrix swaps two rows when multiplied on the left?
How many entries equal to $1$ does a $4\times4$ permutation matrix have?
Is $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$ a permutation matrix?
options: No, because the ones are not all on the main diagonal.
Yes, each row and each column has exactly one $1$.

questions.question: What is $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}$?
Which matrix is not a permutation matrix?
Why is the product of two permutation matrices again a permutation matrix?
options: Matrix multiplication erases the row condition.
Doing two reorderings in succession is still a reordering.
The product always becomes the zero matrix.

questions.question: What is the inverse of a permutation matrix like?
options: Another permutation matrix reversing the order.
It exists only for the identity matrix.
It is always the zero matrix.
It has two ones in each row.

questions.question: Why does a matrix with one $1$ in each row but two $1$s in one column fail to be a permutation matrix?
options: Permutation matrices cannot have off-diagonal ones.
The matrix has too many zeros.
The row condition is stronger than the column condition.
The column condition fails, so two rows map to the same position.

questions.question: Let $P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$. What does $P$ do when multiplied on the left of a $3\times n$ matrix?
Compute $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$.
If $P$ represents the cycle $1\mapsto2$, $2\mapsto3$, $3\mapsto1$, how many ones are in $P$?
Why are permutation matrices useful in LU decomposition with pivoting?
options: They record row interchanges as matrix multiplication.
They turn every matrix into a diagonal matrix.

questions.question: A student says any $0$-$1$ square matrix with exactly $n$ ones is a permutation matrix. What is missing?
options: The ones must be distributed one per row and one per column.
The matrix must be upper triangular.
The matrix must have no zero entries.
The determinant must be written on the diagonal.

questions.question: Let $P=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$. What is $P\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$?
If $P$ swaps rows $1$ and $3$, what is $P^{-1}$?
options: A matrix that swaps columns $1$ and $2$ instead.
